summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY, building embedded robotics systems that span real-time firmware, on-board perception, and the networking that ties them together. Designed COFFIN, a voice-controlled vision-guided manipulator with TensorRT-optimized YOLO visual servoing, ToF contact sensing over I2C, and a WebSocket-linked Jetson + Arduino stack. Comfortable from bare-metal C on Cortex-M up through ROS 2 autonomy and socket/Bluetooth comms.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Built a gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth, translating 3-DoF hand motion into real-time HID commands.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Led a 25-member robotics team, owning mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and AI/ML integration end-to-end.
Designed and fabricated single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Vision-Guided Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Architected a voice-controlled, vision-guided pick-and-place robot as a three-layer distributed system — Flutter client, Flask-SocketIO edge server, and Jetson + Arduino controller linked by a unified WebSocket fabric.

Integrated faster-whisper STT and Gemini intent classification with TensorRT-optimized YOLO visual servoing (5.2× speedup: 56.7→10.9 ms, 17.6→92 FPS) and dual VL53L0X ToF sensors over a TCA9548A I2C mux for contact-aware grasping.

Implemented two-link inverse kinematics on Arduino in C++ driving five servos with range-gated contact detection; debugged 11 integration failures (false detections, servo brown-out, stale frames) to reach 100% pick reliability (10/10) at ~11.5s end-to-end voice-to-picked latency.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Programmed Cortex-M4 peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1) with timer-triggered ADC scan conversions and interrupt-driven sample capture.
Achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate; verified end-to-end in Proteus.

projects.name: ROS-Based Robotic Arm (UR5e & AL5B)
bullets: Derived DH tables and hand-computed forward kinematic chains (0T6) for a 6-DoF UR5e and 5-DoF AL5B; validated against MoveIt/RViz URDF models in ROS 2 Humble and ROS Noetic.
Executed collision-free trajectories on a physical UR5e via the UR ROS 2 driver; AL5B repeatability measured <2 mm over 10 trials.

projects.name: ABB RobotStudio Automation Cell
bullets: Programmed an ABB RobotStudio press-to-packing workcell in RAPID with TCP socket-based pose acquisition and interrupt-driven press-bench logic; validated full-cycle repeatability.
